# Onboard this repo to dev-system

You are onboarding the repo in the current working directory. Follow the procedure below
exactly, step by step, starting with step 0: ask the user the questions there before you
run anything. Links point to the dev-system repo on GitHub, which is the reference for
anything the procedure does not spell out.

Instructions for an agent. Run them in the target folder, whether it is empty or an
existing repo. Run every step; each one says how to check it worked. Background for any step
is in [`architecture.md`](https://github.com/cbundy/dev-system/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) and [`../templates/README.md`](https://github.com/cbundy/dev-system/blob/main/templates/README.md).

With the `callum-flow` plugin installed, `/callum-flow:onboard` gives an agent these same
instructions as a skill (generated from this page, never edited by hand).

## Done when

- `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/factory-loop.json`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`,
  `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`, `.gitignore`, `treehouse.toml`, `.callum-dev.json`
  and `.callum-dev/baseline/` are committed.
- `package.json` has `@callum/dev-system` as a devDependency, from
  `github:cbundy/dev-system#semver:0.x`.
- `grep -rn '<REPLACE' --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.callum-dev .` prints
  nothing.
- `npx callum-dev check` exits 0.
- The checks in [Verify](#5-verify) pass.
- If the user asked for the factory loop (step 7): a loop workspace runs in act mode, and the
  loop has claimed one issue labelled `ready` and merged its PR after CI passed.

## Rules

- Do not edit, copy or vendor anything from `node_modules/@callum/dev-system` into the
  repo by hand, apart from the synced blocks in step 3b. Shared behaviour changes upstream
  through `/update-dev`.
- Do not edit inside `--- synced ---` blocks. Fill in only `--- repo-owned ---` blocks and
  `<REPLACE>` placeholders.
- Use the `base-image` devcontainer. Never use `feature`: it is deprecated
  (cbundy/dev-system#89).
- Never put secrets in the repo, including the agentsview URL. Secrets come from the
  runtime.
- Do not delete or gitignore `.callum-dev.json` or `.callum-dev/baseline/`. Without them,
  `update` cannot merge.
- Ask the user before any outward-facing step: creating a GitHub repo, pushing, creating
  a Coder workspace, changing branch protection, or switching the factory loop to act mode.

## 0. Ask the user first

Get these before running anything. Do not guess them.

| Question | Used in |
|---|---|
| Repo name | devcontainer `name`, the GitHub repo |
| Language and stack, or "decide later" for an empty folder | lint and test commands, `.gitignore` repo-owned block, per-repo Dockerfile |
| Lint command and full test command, if they exist yet | step 3 (commands) |
| GitHub owner and visibility; create the repo now? | step 4 |
| Extra system tools the repo needs (Terraform, a DB client, ...)? Python alone needs none: the base image has uv | step 3e |
| Run it on Coder? With which per-repo image, if any? | step 6 |
| Put it on the factory loop? As the user's own GitHub account or another one? Who else may file work for it (their GitHub logins)? | step 7 |

## 1. Prerequisites

Required: `git`, `node` 18 or later with `npm`, and network access to github.com. `gh`,
logged in, is needed only for step 4.

```bash
git --version && node --version && npm --version
```

Inside a dev-system container all of these are already there.

## 2. Initialise git and npm

Empty folder:

```bash
git init -b main
npm init -y
npm pkg set private=true
```

An existing repo keeps its own git history. If it has no `package.json`, create one as
above, even for a project that does not use Node: the file only carries the dev-system
dependency.

Then:

```bash
npm i -D github:cbundy/dev-system#semver:0.x
```

Check: `npx callum-dev --version` prints a version.

## 3. Scaffold the config

### Settle the commands first

Every agent, every sub-agent, the factory loop's gate and CI run these commands, often many
times per change. Get them right before writing any file. Start from the commands the repo
really uses (`package.json` scripts, `Makefile`, `pyproject.toml`, CI workflows, the README)
and run each to confirm it works.

**Why it matters.** Everything a gate prints lands in an agent's context, on every run. A
suite that prints a line per passing test costs thousands of lines a run, multiplied by
every sub-agent, every gate retry and every agent that reads the gate output. An
ambiguous or multi-step gate makes agents improvise their own commands, run gates piecemeal
and skip some. A gate that passes with warnings scrolling past teaches agents to ignore
output, and then they miss the real failure.

**The contract.** Each gate (lint, typecheck, test, e2e if there is one) gets exactly one
command that:

- runs from the repo root, non-interactively, and gives the same result every time. Its
  exit code is the verdict: 0 passes, anything else fails.
- covers the whole gate. If a gate is spread across several commands or directories, add
  a single entrypoint (an npm script, a make target or a `scripts/` file) that runs them
  all, so a new test file needs no extra wiring.
  Have the test entrypoint also accept a subset (for example `npm test -- <path>`), so an
  agent debugging one suite runs it through the same setup instead of a raw runner command.
- is quiet on success: one summary line at most. No per-test pass lines, progress bars,
  banners or coverage tables, and no log lines that tests trigger on purpose.
- on failure prints only what is needed to act: the failing test names or `file:line`, and
  the assertion or error.
- has that behaviour built in, in the command itself or the tool's config file (reporter,
  `addopts`, ...), never in a flag an agent has to remember, so the agent, the loop and
  CI all see the same output.
- treats warnings as failures, or turns the rule off. A warning that passes is noise.
- works in a fresh worktree with no dependencies installed, which is what the factory
  loop's slot and a CI checkout are. Either the command installs what it needs, or the
  install step goes in front of it, e.g. `npm ci && npm run test`.

A combined `check` command that runs the fast gates in order and stops at the first
failure (auto-fixers such as a formatter first) is worth adding: an agent then verifies a
change in one call before handoff. If e2e is slow, decide which gate runs it (the loop's gate
or CI) and when an agent should run it locally.

Write exactly these commands into the three places that carry them, with nothing added
except the install step: `.claude/factory-loop.json` `gateCommands` (the factory loop's stop
gate, `[<lint>, <test>]`), `CLAUDE.md` "Canonical commands" and the lint and test steps of
`.github/workflows/ci.yml`. The agent's brief, the loop's gate and CI then cannot drift. If a
gate has no command yet, say so to the user rather than inventing one.

Examples only; adapt them to the repo and check the options against the installed version:

| Tool | Quiet on success, failures only |
|---|---|
| Node `node:test` | `node --test --test-reporter=dot` |
| Vitest | `reporters: ['dot']` and `silent: true` in the config |
| Bun | `onlyFailures = true` under `[test]` in `bunfig.toml` |
| Playwright | `reporter: 'dot'` in the config (keep `html` as a second reporter for digging in) |
| pytest | `addopts = "-q --tb=short"` in `pyproject.toml` |
| Go | `go test ./...` without `-v`: one `ok` line per package, failures in full |
| ESLint | `eslint . --max-warnings=0`: nothing when clean, warnings fail |
| ShellCheck | `shellcheck -f gcc <files>`: one `file:line:col` line per finding, nothing when clean |

**Check it.** Run each command twice and report both results to the user:

1. On the clean tree: exit 0, and at most a few lines of output.
2. With a deliberately failing test (for the test gate) or lint error (for the lint gate):
   non-zero exit, and a few lines that name the file, the test and the error. Then revert
   the breakage.

If either output is long, fix the tool's config before going on.

### 3a. Run init

`init` reads three answers from stdin, one per line: repo name, lint command, test
command. A blank line leaves a `<REPLACE>` placeholder in place.

```bash
printf '%s\n' "<repo name>" "<lint command>" "<test command>" \
  | npx callum-dev init --devcontainer base-image
```

It prints `created` or `skipped` for each file, and lists the files that still have
placeholders. If `.callum-dev.json` already exists, init refuses to run. The repo is already
onboarded: run `npx callum-dev update` instead and stop here.

### 3b. Merge files that init skipped (existing repos only)

init never overwrites an existing file. For each file reported as `skipped`, typically
`CLAUDE.md` and `.gitignore`:

1. Open the template, `node_modules/@callum/dev-system/templates/<file>`. For `.gitignore`
   the template is `templates/gitignore`, with no dot.
2. Copy its `--- synced ---` block into the repo's file verbatim, markers included, so a
   later `update` can find and merge it.
3. Wrap the repo's existing content in a `--- repo-owned ---` block, in the positions the
   template uses. In `.gitignore` the repo-owned block goes at the **bottom**.
4. For `.claude/settings.json`, keep the template's keys exactly, add the repo's own
   entries to the end of `permissions.allow`, and keep any keys of the repo's own that the
   template does not have.

### 3c. Fill every placeholder

```bash
grep -rn '<REPLACE' --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.callum-dev .
```

| File | Placeholder | Fill with |
|---|---|---|
| `.claude/factory-loop.json` | `gateCommands` (lint, then test) | The commands from "Settle the commands first", working in a **fresh worktree with no dependencies installed**: include the install step, e.g. `npm ci && npm run lint`. With no tests yet, use a command that exits 0 and say so to the user. Init fills them from its prompts. |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | toolchain-and-install step, lint and test `run:` lines | The toolchain setup and install the commands need, and the same lint and test commands as `gateCommands` (step 3f) |
| `CLAUDE.md` | e2e visual verification doc path | The repo's UI screenshot doc. For a repo with no UI, replace it with `n/a - no UI`. |
| `CLAUDE.md` | `## Canonical commands` | The commands from "Settle the commands first", one per gate, the same as `gateCommands` minus the install step, and which CI job calls each (the real job names from `ci.yml`, step 3f) |
| `CLAUDE.md` | worktree mechanism | `a treehouse worktree` unless the user says otherwise |
| `CLAUDE.md` | repo-specific variations | Extra build or boot steps before the app can run, or delete the line |
| `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` | `remoteEnv` example | Delete the comment line, or add real env vars, e.g. `"DEV_LOGIN_TOOLS": "claude,gh"` for a repo that never uses codex |

Leave `treehouse.toml` as it is unless the user says otherwise.

### 3d. Repo-owned `.gitignore` entries

Add the stack's own build output, local databases and generated files to the bottom
repo-owned block. Check each rule with `git check-ignore -v <path>`.

### 3e. Per-repo image (only if the repo needs extra tools)

A Python repo does not need one just for Python. The base image's `python3` has no `pip`
or `venv`, but it ships uv: write the gates as `uv run --with pytest pytest` (or
`uv run pytest` when the repo has a `pyproject.toml`) and `uvx ruff check .`, and uv
installs what they need on first run. Add a per-repo image only for system tools uv
cannot provide.

Otherwise, create `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`:

```dockerfile
FROM ghcr.io/cbundy/dev-system/base:2
USER root
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends <packages> \
  && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
# Release stamp, so `dev-version` can tell whether this image is current. Set
# IMAGE to the image your CI publishes, pass the three build args from CI, and
# set TAG to the tag workspaces pull.
ARG VERSION=dev
ARG REVISION=unknown
ARG CREATED=unknown
RUN mkdir -p /usr/local/share/dev-system/image-release.d \
  && printf '%s\n' \
    "IMAGE=ghcr.io/<owner>/<repo>/dev" \
    "VERSION=${VERSION}" \
    "REVISION=${REVISION}" \
    "CREATED=${CREATED}" \
    "TAG=latest" \
    > /usr/local/share/dev-system/image-release.d/dev \
  && chmod 0644 /usr/local/share/dev-system/image-release.d/dev
USER node
```

In `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`, replace `"image": ...` with
`"build": { "dockerfile": "Dockerfile" }`. Do not change `ENTRYPOINT`, add a `VOLUME`,
install anything under `/persist`, or set a `devcontainer.metadata` label. See
[Extending the image](https://github.com/cbundy/dev-system/blob/main/images/base/README.md#extending-the-image).

### 3f. CI workflow

Do this after the `gateCommands` are final. Without a workflow, a PR gets no checks.

1. If `.github/workflows/` already has a CI workflow, keep it and delete the scaffolded
   `ci.yml` and its baseline copy `.callum-dev/baseline/.github/workflows/ci.yml` (while the
   baseline exists, `callum-dev update` restores a deleted `ci.yml`), after checking that it runs the same lint and test commands as `gateCommands`
   (fix it if not). Otherwise fill the scaffolded `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
2. In the scaffolded `ci.yml`:
   - Replace the toolchain-and-install step with what the gate commands need (for example
     `actions/setup-node` and `npm ci`, or `astral-sh/setup-uv`), or delete it if none.
   - Confirm the lint and test steps run exactly the `gateCommands` (init filled them from
     its prompts).
3. Put the real job name(s) from `ci.yml` in the `CLAUDE.md` "Canonical commands" note on
   which CI job runs each gate.

Pushing a workflow file needs a gh token with the `workflow` scope. If a push is refused
for that, `dev-doctor` shows a WARN with the fix: `gh auth refresh -h github.com -s workflow`.

A PR opened before `ci.yml` reaches the default branch gets no checks until a new
`pull_request` event (push a commit, or close and reopen it).

### 3g. Release workflow (only if the repo cuts releases from its own workflow)

Skip this when the repo does not create GitHub Releases in a workflow. Otherwise add one step
after the step that creates the Release, so its `released` event reaches the factory store:

```yaml
- uses: cbundy/dev-system/.github/actions/released-event@vX.Y.Z   # the dev-system release you use
  env:
    GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}   # the job needs `contents: write`
  with:
    tag: ${{ steps.release.outputs.tag }}   # the tag the Release was created for
```

The step attaches `factory-released.json` to the Release. A device running the factory push loop
collects it: set `FACTORY_RELEASE_REPOS=owner/name` on the device for a repo it has never logged an
event for (a repo it already has a factory log for is watched without it).

### Existing consumers

A repo onboarded before the factory-loop-only setup keeps its files. `npx callum-dev update`
now:

- prints `unsynced` for each file of a retired template, leaves it untouched and stops syncing
  it, and keeps the retired template's entries in `.claude/settings.json` `permissions.allow`
  (they are repo-owned from then on; delete them if unused). Which files and entries these are is
  in [the templates README, "Retired templates"](https://github.com/cbundy/dev-system/blob/main/templates/README.md#retired-templates);
- prints `new` for `.claude/factory-loop.json` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` when the repo has
  neither, and does not create them (a placeholder CI workflow would fail the repo's PRs). To
  adopt them, copy the template from `node_modules/@callum/dev-system/templates/` and fill it in
  as in steps 3c and 3f.

## 4. Commit (and GitHub, if the user said yes)

```bash
git add -A
git status --short   # must include .github/workflows/ci.yml, .callum-dev.json and .callum-dev/; must not include node_modules/, .env, settings.local.json
git commit -m "chore: onboard to dev-system"
```

Only if the user agreed in step 0:

```bash
gh repo create <owner>/<name> --<private|public> --source . --push
```

The push includes `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, so the gh token needs the `workflow` scope
(see step 3f).

## 5. Verify

Run all of these and report each result.

```bash
npx callum-dev check
node -e 'JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(".claude/settings.json","utf8"))'
node -e 'const c=JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(".claude/factory-loop.json","utf8")); if(!Array.isArray(c.gateCommands)||c.gateCommands.length<1) throw new Error("no gateCommands")'
grep -rn '<REPLACE' --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.callum-dev . || echo "no placeholders"
test -f .github/workflows/ci.yml && echo "ci.yml present" || echo "BAD: no ci.yml (step 3f)"
git check-ignore -v .claude/factory-loop.json .callum-dev.json .callum-dev/baseline/CLAUDE.md && echo "BAD: tracked file ignored" || echo ok
```

Once committed, run the `gateCommands` in a fresh worktree, the way the loop's slot does,
then remove it:

```bash
git worktree add --detach ../gatecheck-tmp
(cd ../gatecheck-tmp && <gateCommands[0]> && <gateCommands[1]>)
git worktree remove --force ../gatecheck-tmp
```

If the agent is running inside a dev-system container, also run `dev-init --repo` and
then `dev-doctor`. Login failures are expected until the user logs in. Report any other
`FAIL`.

Also check that the lint and test commands match across the three places: `gateCommands` in
`.claude/factory-loop.json`, `CLAUDE.md` "Canonical commands" and `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. After the first push (step 4), confirm the CI job shows up: `gh pr checks`
on the PR, or `gh run list --branch <default branch>`.

## 6. Run it on Coder (if the user said yes)

Needs the `coder` CLI logged in, the repo pushed (step 4), and the `dev-system` template
on the Coder server. The template, its parameters and first-run logins are documented in
the [Coder template README](https://github.com/cbundy/dev-system/blob/main/coder/dev-system/README.md).

```bash
coder create <name> --template dev-system --parameter repo_url=<https clone url>
```

- Remote Control mode `auto` (the default) becomes `server` when there is a repo: each
  session started in claude.ai gets its own worktree.
- A private repo needs a GitHub credential before the clone works: Coder external auth, or
  the gh login on the Log in page. To run the workspace as another GitHub account (a loop
  for someone else's repo), see the README section "Working a repo as another GitHub account".
- A repo with a per-repo image (step 3e) must have that image built and pushed to a
  registry, then passed with `--parameter image=<image>`. A private image needs registry
  credentials on the template (README, "Private images").

Then the user opens the workspace in the Coder dashboard, clicks **Log in** and signs in
to Claude (and codex and gh). Within 30s the workspace shows up in claude.ai. Check with
`coder ssh <name> -- dev-login status`, and `coder ssh <name> -- dev-doctor` once logged in.

## 7. Put the repo on the factory loop (if the user said yes)

The factory loop is how factory work gets done: a plugin in its own Coder workspace that claims
issues labelled `ready`, has agents design, build, review and fix each one in its own worktree,
and merges the PR once CI passes. It wakes Claude only for judgment calls and to speak to the
owner. This workspace is separate from the step 6 one, which stays for hand-driven sessions. The
workspace itself is documented in the Coder README,
[Loop orchestrator workspace](https://github.com/cbundy/dev-system/blob/main/coder/dev-system/README.md#loop-orchestrator-workspace).

Needs steps 3 to 5 done and pushed, the `coder` CLI logged in, and the `orchestrator-loop`
template on the Coder server.

### What the loop needs from the repo

- **Gate commands** in `.claude/factory-loop.json` `gateCommands` (step 3). When a builder or a
  fixer finishes, the loop's stop gate runs them in that agent's worktree and refuses the finish
  while one fails
  ([factory-loop-workspace](https://github.com/cbundy/dev-system/blob/main/plugins/factory-loop-workspace/README.md), "What it does"). The loop
  reads this file from the default branch on GitHub, not from the checkout, so a change applies
  once it is merged.
- **The same commands in a GitHub CI workflow** (step 3f). The merge queue merges a PR only when
  it has at least one check and every check on its head passed or was skipped. GitHub CI is the
  only test gate before merge; there is no local pipeline.
- **Branch protection** on the default branch that requires the CI check, as a backstop, with
  "Require branches to be up to date" on. Do not require approving reviews: the loop's reviewer
  is an agent, not a GitHub review, and the loop's account cannot approve its own PRs. With the
  user's go-ahead (job `ci` from the scaffolded workflow; use the real job name):

  ```bash
  gh api -X PUT repos/<owner>/<repo>/branches/<default branch>/protection --input - <<'EOF'
  {"required_status_checks":{"strict":true,"contexts":["ci"]},"enforce_admins":false,
   "required_pull_request_reviews":null,"restrictions":null}
  EOF
  ```

  GitHub refuses this on a private repo of a free plan. The merge queue's own check rule then
  stands alone; say so to the user.
- **A `ready` label**, which is how the user hands the loop an issue. The loop creates its own
  `factory:*` labels; `ready` it does not:
  `gh label create ready --repo <owner>/<repo> --description "Ready for the factory loop" --force`.

### Settings

The settings a repo usually sets in `.claude/factory-loop.json`:

| Setting | Default | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| `gateCommands` | `[]` | The stop gate's commands, run in order in the agent's worktree (lint, then test). Empty means no gate. |
| `gateTimeoutMs` | `10m` | The budget for all of the gate commands together, in milliseconds (or `gateTimeout` as a duration, like `"15m"`). A gate that runs out is recorded as unknown, never as a pass, and CI decides. |
| `maxInFlightIssues` | `3` | How many issues the loop works on at once. Parked and waiting issues do not count. The loop also holds fewer when the container's memory cannot hold that many (see `slotMemoryMiB`). |
| `slotMemoryMiB` | `auto` | The memory one issue's slot is assumed to use, in MiB. `auto` measures it from the stop gates' memory and uses 3072 until three runs are measured. The container's memory less `memoryReserveMiB`, over this, is the most issues held at once. |
| `memoryReserveMiB` | `2048` | The container's memory kept free of slots, in MiB. |
| `uiCapture` | unset | The repo's documented, self-stopping UI capture command (like `"npm run e2e:capture --"`), which builders and fixers run first for a visible change; or `"none"` when the repo has no capture tooling, so the reviewer treats a missing screenshot as a warning, not an error. Unset keeps a missing capture an error. |
| `skipLabels` | `[]` | Labels that keep an issue from being claimed even when it is `ready`. |
| `minimumReleaseCadence` | `6h` | For a repo that releases: the longest the judge lets merged work wait for a release, at least `1h`. |
| `releaseBranchPrefix` | `none` | The branch prefix of a release's bump PR (like `"chore/release-"`). While such a PR is open the merge queue holds its merges, so the bump PR's CI is not preempted. Unset turns the hold off. |
| `releaseHold` | `45m` | The longest the queue holds per push of the bump PR while its checks are pending or green, counted from the head's start (commit or first check); a push restarts it and a failed check ends it; `0` turns the hold off. |

`/factory help config` lists every setting with its default and a one-line meaning, and
[the v2 SPEC, appendix A](https://github.com/cbundy/dev-system/blob/main/docs/factory-loop/v2/SPEC.md#appendix-a-settings) has the full table. The
workspace file, `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR}/factory-loop/config.json` (`/persist/claude/factory-loop/config.json`
in a Coder workspace), can set any key and wins over the repo's file. `/factory config` shows
every setting the loop runs with and where each came from.

### Create the loop workspace

```bash
coder create <repo>-loop --template orchestrator-loop \
  --parameter repo_url=<https clone url> \
  --parameter remote_control_skip_permissions=true \
  --parameter cpus=8
```

- **Skip permissions.** The loop's agents run unattended, so a tool call that would ask for
  approval is refused instead (v2 SPEC 10.10). Every loop workspace in use runs with
  `remote_control_skip_permissions=true`. It is the user's call: confirm it with them.
- **CPUs.** The stop gate runs one full gate per 8 CPUs at once (`gateConcurrency` `auto`), and
  the template's default of 2 also has to carry the agents. 8 or more keeps several issues
  moving.
- **Logins, private repos and per-repo images** are as in step 6: **Log in** in the dashboard,
  a GitHub credential for a private repo, and `--parameter image=<image>` for a per-repo image.
- **Another GitHub account.** To run the loop as someone else's account (a loop for their repo),
  follow the Coder README,
  [Working a repo as another GitHub account](https://github.com/cbundy/dev-system/blob/main/coder/dev-system/README.md#working-a-repo-as-another-github-account).

Once logged in, the workspace shows up in claude.ai as `🏭 <repo> loop`: that session is the
loop's judge, and where the user talks to the factory.

### Trusted authors

The loop claims only issues opened by a trusted author, and reads only trusted authors' comments,
so an answer to a parked issue counts only from one. The list is the template's
`trusted_authors`, plus the workspace's `extra_trusted_authors` parameter for the repo owner and
collaborators, as `login:id` entries (look an id up with `gh api users/<login> --jq .id`). In
token mode the token's own account is trusted too. `coder ssh <repo>-loop -- dev-doctor` shows the
effective list.

### Observe first, then act

The loop starts in observe mode: every minute it reads the repo, plans and logs what it would do,
and does nothing. In the loop's session:

1. `/factory status` shows the last pass and what it would do. Check that it names the right repo
   and sees the `ready` queue.
2. With the user's go-ahead, `/factory mode act` switches it on from the next pass.
3. Confirm it acts. Every pass writes one line to the decision log, which says whether it acted
   (`executed`) and, while a safety rail fails, why not (`rails`). Inside the workspace
   (`coder ssh <repo>-loop`):

   ```bash
   tail -n 1 "$(ls -t /persist/claude/factory-loop/<owner>__<repo>/decisions-*.jsonl | head -n 1)" \
     | jq '{mode, executed, rails}'
   ```

   `"executed": true` with no `rails` means it acts. While any rail fails it keeps observing
   (see Troubleshooting below).

### Feeding it

- **Label an issue `ready`.** The loop claims it and moves it through its labels:
  `factory:queued`, `factory:designing`, `factory:building`, `factory:reviewing`,
  `factory:fixing` and `factory:merge-queue`, then closes it when its PR merges.
- **`factory:parked`** means it waits on the owner. Answer the question on the issue, then
  remove the label to resume (or `/factory resume <N> "<note>"`).
- **`factory:waiting`** means it waits on something the loop checks itself, such as another
  issue closing. It resumes by itself.
- **`factory:rejected`** means its last life ended without a merge: after 3 tries the loop
  gives up on it. Remove the label and add `ready` to try again.

### Steering it

`/factory <op>` from the loop's session (or ask in chat):

| Op | What it does |
|---|---|
| `status` | the last pass and the directives in force |
| `config` | every setting the loop runs with, and its source |
| `priority <N...>` / `only <N...>` | claim these first / claim only these (`off` clears either) |
| `skip <N>` / `pause <N>` | never claim N / take no action on N (`noskip`, `unpause` undo them) |
| `new off` | claim and start nothing new; work in flight goes on (`new on` undoes it) |
| `note [<N>] <text>\|off` | an instruction for N's next agent, or for every issue's; a newer note replaces the older one, off clears it |
| `resume <N> ["<note>"]` | unpark N |
| `drop <N>` | abandon N for this life; its agents stop and its claim is released |
| `mode off\|observe\|act` | stop, watch only, or work |

`/factory help` lists every op, `/factory help config` every setting, and [the v2 SPEC, appendix E](https://github.com/cbundy/dev-system/blob/main/docs/factory-loop/v2/SPEC.md#appendix-e-owner-ops)
says what each does. To stop the loop within a minute whatever its mode, create the `OFF` file
in the workspace: `touch /persist/claude/factory-loop/OFF`, and delete it to start again.

### The first run

Label one small, well-described issue `ready` and watch it go from claimed to designed (a brief
comment on the issue), built, PR opened, CI, reviewed and merged. The labels show where it is,
`/factory status` shows what the loop is doing, and the `factory-state` skill
(`/callum-flow:factory-state`) shows the factory as a whole, stuck issues included.

### Troubleshooting

| Symptom | What shows it | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Act mode does nothing: the role | `rails`: `role: DEV_ROLE is dev, act needs orchestrator` | The workspace is not from the `orchestrator-loop` template. Create one from it. |
| Act mode does nothing: another orchestrator | `rails`: `heartbeat: another orchestrator on this repo is up (<device> ...)` | Another orchestrator workspace runs on the repo. Stop it: one loop per repo. A beat from this loop's own Coder workspace under another device name never blocks; it shows as `railTwins`. |
| Act mode does nothing: the act lock | `rails`: `act lock: session <id> holds it until <time>` | Another session in this workspace holds the loop. Close it; the lock frees itself when its lease runs out. |
| Act mode does nothing: the factory database | `rails`: `heartbeat: query failed (...)` | The workspace cannot query the factory database. `coder ssh <repo>-loop -- dev-doctor` shows its database checks, with the fix for each. |
| Act mode does nothing: the repo | `rails`: `repo: the checkout ... is ..., not <owner>/<repo>` | The checkout's `origin` is another repo. Fix `repo_url`, or `repo` in the workspace file. |
| Issues are claimed but no agent starts | a `workspace` notice in the session; skipped lines `workspace: ...; agent steps are held` in the decision log | The companion plugin `factory-loop-workspace` is not loaded. Bring the workspace up to date with the template (it installs it), or install it, then restart the session. |
| Builders finish without running the gates | `/factory config` shows `gateCommands none`; no `gate-pass` or `gate-fail` lines in `/persist/claude/factory-loop/<owner>__<repo>/companion.jsonl` | Set `gateCommands` in `.claude/factory-loop.json` and merge it to the default branch. |
| A PR stays in `factory:reviewing`, then goes to triage or parks | the PR has no checks on GitHub | CI does not run on pull requests. Fix the workflow (step 3f) and merge it to the default branch. The loop waits 10 minutes (`ciStartMs`) for a check to start before it counts the step as failed, and never merges a PR with no checks. |

## 8. Tell the user

Report:

- what was created and what was merged,
- the commands you chose, their clean and deliberately broken output, and any command you
  could not determine,
- if step 7 ran: the loop workspace's name, its mode, and the first issue it merged (or where
  that issue is now),
- what the user still has to do, with the commands:

| Next step | How |
|---|---|
| Open it on the desktop | Reopen in Container (VS Code) or `devcontainer up --workspace-folder .`. Then log in once: `dev-login start`. |
| Run it in Coder | Step 6, if not done: `coder create <name> --template dev-system --parameter repo_url=<https clone url>`, then **Log in** in the dashboard. |
| Put it on the factory loop | Step 7, if not done: the repo's branch protection and `ready` label, a workspace from the `orchestrator-loop` template ("Create the loop workspace"), **Log in**, `/factory mode act` in its session, and one issue labelled `ready`. |
| Hand the loop work | Label an issue `ready`. Answer a `factory:parked` issue on the issue, then remove the label. `/factory help` in the loop's session lists the controls. |
| Enable the workflow plugin | The base image's `dev-init` installs `callum-flow@callum` by default on every container start, on the desktop and in Coder. See [Claude plugins](https://github.com/cbundy/dev-system/blob/main/images/base/README.md#workspace-and-repo) for opt-outs and recovery when an install fails. |
| Session history (agentsview) | Nothing per repo. The URL is set once per host (`images/base/README.md`, "Central session history"). |
| Keep in sync later | `npm update @callum/dev-system && npx callum-dev update`, then commit. Optionally add `npx callum-dev check` to the `ci.yml` from step 3f. |
